nwrspeciesr

Overview

nwrspeciesr is an R interface to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service National Wildlife Refuge System species occurrence database (NWRSpecies, formerly FWSpecies). It supports retrieval of refuge species data and experimental authenticated upload operations.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("USFWS/nwrspeciesr")

The fwsunitr dependency is installed automatically.

Usage

Getting refuge species data

Use get_species_list() to retrieve species occurrence records with optional filters for region, refuge, taxonomic category, occurrence, and ITIS TSN. Use download_species_list() to retrieve the CSV download endpoint, including large responses saved directly to a file. The lookup functions return valid category and occurrence values.

library(nwrspeciesr)

get_species_list(
  region_number = 7,
  category_name = "Bird",
  occurrence = "Present"
)

get_species_list(refuge_code = "FF07RKDK00")
get_species_categories()
get_species_occurrences()

download_species_list(
  refuge_code = "FF07RKDK00",
  rows_per_page = 130000,
  path = "species-list.csv"
)

Refuges can also be selected by name. Matching is case-insensitive and tolerant of common variants such as “Kenai”, “kenai nwr”, and “Kenai National Wildlife Refuge”:

get_species_list(refuge_name = "kenai nwr")

By default, get_species_list() uses a copy of the refuge name-to-code crosswalk included with the package. This copy may not reflect the latest changes to refuge names or codes. To retrieve the current crosswalk from the FWS Unit API, run get_refuges() and pass the result to crosswalk:

current_refuges <- get_refuges()
get_species_list(refuge_name = "Kenai", crosswalk = current_refuges)

Only the public SpeciesListBasic method is exposed by the public API. Sensitive species and records with a Draft status are never returned. Ambiguous refuge names return an informative error listing the candidates.

Uploading refuge species data

The package provides experimental functions for authenticated write access through the internal SpeciesUpload API:

  • get_upload_permissions(): list refuges writable with the API key.
  • create_species_record(): create one record.
  • create_species_records(): create up to 200 records in one batch request.
  • replace_species_record(): fully replace one existing record.
  • replace_species_records(): fully replace up to 25 existing records in one all-or-nothing batch request.
  • add_species_evidence(): add URL evidence to a record.

Replacement is a full replacement, not a partial update. Include every field that should remain on the record, including status, refugeAccepted, and isSensitive. Use the single-record function for one record; use the batch function when multiple records should be replaced together.

Set the API key in the NWRSPECIES_API_KEY environment variable, or pass it explicitly with api_key. The upload API defaults to the staging server at https://staging-iris.fws.gov/APPS/SpeciesAPI/api/ while the service is under testing. These functions can modify NWRSpecies data, so verify permissions and payloads before sending requests.

Sys.setenv(NWRSPECIES_API_KEY = "your-api-key")

permissions <- get_upload_permissions()

created <- create_species_record(
  list(
    refugeCode = permissions$refugeCode[[1]],
    taxonCode = 93710
  )
)

add_species_evidence(list(
  speciesId = created$speciesId,
  url = "https://example.gov/report/123",
  observationDate = "2026-05-14",
  datePrecisionId = 1,
  photograph = TRUE
))

Do not commit API keys to scripts or repositories. For batch limits and complete field validation rules, see the function documentation and the upload user guide included in the repository.
